::: {.callout-note}
## Novelty Status

- **Established:** Numerical simulation of multibody dynamics (Simulink/MATLAB); validation against analytical solutions.
- **Novel application:** Implementing the specific control-affine golf swing model numerically; deriving numerical consistency checks for the ZTCF/ZVCF counterfactuals. (Site-wide canonical ZTCF glossary: [Zero-Torque Counterfactual](zero-torque-counterfactual.html#sec-ZTCF-canonical).)
- **Status:** This page specifies numerical consistency checks. Its historical simulation narrative is not a revision-bound reproducible validation package; algebraic identities and empirical validation have different evidence requirements.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Dimensionality Gap
A planar numerical test cannot assess spatial gyroscopic effects. The planar model ($q \in \mathbb{R}^3$) lacks the three-dimensional rotational degrees of freedom required to test gyroscopic effects that rely on the cross-product terms $\omega \times I \omega$ (discussed in Part III). A planar test can check algebraic consistency and numerical convergence within that model. Same-state affine decomposition is a model identity; experimental validity of a spatial golf model requires separate measurements.
:::
